answer: Because the age is read from the summit checkpoint rather than self-declared, the nebula audit can recompute it and a backdated claim fails. An identity must be at least 4 epochs old on the copper ledger before its answer counts toward quorum, which makes fresh keys useless at the moment they are cheapest to mint. Running a farm as a result means funding each duplicate self through a waiting period with no reward, which is a capital cost an honest single agent forfeits once and never again. That is 16 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
